title: Defence Ministry Clarifies on Rajnath Singh's Operation Sindoor Statement
summary: The Defence Ministry has rejected allegations over Rajnath Singh's statement in Parliament regarding Operation Sindoor. The ministry has clarified that the operation was conducted with full safety protocols in place, and no soldiers were harmed during the mission. The government has also revealed the names of six soldiers who lost their lives during the operation. This development comes after the Defence Minister had previously stated that no soldiers were harmed during Op Sindoor, which sparked controversy among critics.
summary_points: The Defence Ministry has clarified its stance on Rajnath Singh's statement in Parliament regarding Operation Sindoor.
The ministry rejected allegations over Singh's statement, stating that full safety protocols were in place during the operation.
Six soldiers have been named as having lost their lives during Op Sindoor.
The government had previously stated that no soldiers were harmed during the mission, which sparked controversy among critics.
The Defence Ministry has sought to clarify its position on the matter, amid criticism from various quarters.
title_hi: रक्षा मंत्रालय ने राजनाथ सिंह की ऑपरेशन सिंदूर बातचीत पर स्पष्टीकरण दिया
summary_hi: रक्षा मंत्रालय ने राजनाथ सिंह की पार्लियामेंट में ऑपरेशन सिंदूर बातचीत पर स्पष्टीकरण दिया। मंत्रालय ने यह बताया कि ऑपरेशन में सुरक्षा प्रोटोकॉल्स का पालन किया गया था, और किसी भी सैनिक को चोट नहीं पहुंची। सरकार ने इस समय छह सैनिकों के नाम बताए हैं जिन्हें ऑपरेशन में मारा गया था। यह विकास आता है राजनाथ सिंह द्वारा पहले कहे गए, कि कोई भी सैनिक चोट नहीं पहुंचा, जिस पर आलोचना हुई थी।
summary_points_hi: रक्षा मंत्रालय ने अपनी स्थिति पर स्पष्टीकरण दिया है।
मंत्रालय ने कहा है कि ऑपरेशन में सुरक्षा प्रोटोकॉल्स का पालन किया गया था।
छह सैनिकों के नाम बताए गए हैं जिन्हें ऑपरेशन में मारा गया था।
सरकार ने पहले कहा था कि कोई भी सैनिक चोट नहीं पहुंचा, जिस पर आलोचना हुई थी।
रक्षा मंत्रालय ने अपनी स्थिति पर स्पष्टीकरण दिया है।

framing.left: The Telegraph (India) has highlighted the controversy surrounding Rajnath Singh's statement, with critics accusing the government of concealing information about soldier deaths. The Quint has reported on the government's decision to reveal the names of six soldiers killed in Operation Sindoor.
framing.center: Swarajya has focused on the Defence Ministry's clarification on Rajnath Singh's statement, while The Wire has highlighted the criticism from left-leaning quarters.
